title: Conversation Context Strategies — Sunrise Notes
content:
Purpose
- Quick morning brain dump on conversation context strategies that keep showing up in papers and chat with infra/product folks. Not polished — scope: what to try next sprint, measured tradeoffs that matter to Redwood product (latency, cost, regen rate, hallucinations).

High-level takeaways (fast)
- Hybrid windowing + retrieval beats raw long-window decoding for many dialog tasks: keep recent dense context + retrieve sparse long-term memories.
- Latent compression (learned summaries) often reduces token cost but needs careful eval for response fidelity; we must tie to our quality SLO.
- KV-sharding + partial evictions are promising but interact badly with dynamic batching (cache misses = tail latency).

Papers / links skimmed this morning
- "Temporal Retrieval for Dialog Memory" (arXiv:2802.04567) — retrieval policy conditioned on dialog act improved grounding by ~9% but increased median latency 20ms with naive fetch.
- "Lossy Episodic Compression for Long Conversations" (NeurIPS 2027 short) — trained compressor yields 3-4x token reduction, small degradation on factual Qs unless retriever rechecks full text.
- Blog: "Cost-aware Caching for LLM Serving" — practical heuristics for eviction and TTL that correlate with per-token savings.

Notes on applicability to Redwood products
- Hosted API: simplest win is server-side light compression for very long sessions ( > 16k tokens) + automatic OOM-safe fallback. Needs opt-in billing flag.
- Dedicated/Private: allow user-configurable retention window + optional periodic checkpoint uploads to customer's store; integrate with existing Private KMS audit trail.
- Optimize: add a recommendation that flags sessions with "high retrieval churn" and suggests longer in-memory retention or warm caches.

Risks I keep seeing
- Compression-induced hallucinations (especially in multi-turn clarifications). We need evals that measure divergence in clarifying Q/A scenarios, not just static QA F1.
- Hidden cost of retrieval IO: small per-request fetches at scale are non-linear with respect to tail-percentile latency.
- Model drift: summaries that depend on the model's own decoding may encode its hallucinated facts.

Experiment matrix (rough)
- Goal metrics: 95p latency, median latency, tokens/server-charge, regressed QA fidelity on a curated prompt set (clarify-set v1).
- Arms:
  1) Baseline: sliding last-N tokens (N tuned to cost target)
  2) Hybrid: last-M tokens (M small) + sparse retriever top-K from long history (K=3..10)
  3) Compressed: learned compression checkpoint every T turns + hybrid retrieval from compressed store + occasional full-check on mismatch
  4) KV-evict: aggressive KV eviction policy + background prefetch for active sessions
- Workload: mix of short chat (<=2 turns), medium (3–15 turns), long ( > 50 turns). Weighted to mirror product telemetry: ~70% short, 25% medium, 5% long.
- Evaluation: automated rollout on dedicated pool with canary and A/B (feature flag via pr/1234), collect per-route quality metrics and token costs.

Practical infra notes (what will break)
- Batching: hybrid approaches need synchronous retrieval step which reduces batchability; consider async prefetch and cheap approximate retriever (FAISS on compressed embeddings) to avoid blocking.
- Cache invalidation: user edits to prior messages — we need versioning or edit logs, else cached summaries lead to stale grounding.
- Telemetry: add trace points for cache hit/miss, retrieval latency, compression ratio, and fidelity check failures (link these in Console per-route dashboards). 

Short TODOs (for next week)
- [ ] Create clarify-set v1 (20 prompts across 5 domains) — ping Aisha for examples.
- [ ] Prototype compressed-store pipeline (simple seq2seq compressor finetuned on chat transcripts) — baseline script and dataset pointer in repo.
- [ ] Add cache hit/miss counters to serving runtime branch PR #1234 (assign to Mira).
- [ ] Draft Confluence page summarizing risk matrix + rollout safety checklist (start CONF-9876 update).

Questions to discuss with product/solutions
- What SLOs do we guarantee for very long sessions? Are customers okay with an explicit "background retrieval" period for extended history?
- Pricing: do we bill compressed tokens differently? If compression is lossy and leads to quality steps, how do we reflect that?

Open thoughts / heuristics to test
- Keep the last 1–2 turns verbatim, compress windows older than N turns, retrieve 2-3 high-similarity chunks if a retrieval score crosses threshold.
- Use cheap embedding distance delta as a sentinel: if new message is within epsilon of previous context, skip heavy retrieval.
- Use lightweight model (quantized student) to recompute compressed-summary fidelity before using as context for a larger model.

Notes-to-self (random)
- Talk to infra about pre-warmed ephemeral retrievers on the same host as a pool to cut RTTs in half.
- Add example billing vignette for product ("what happens when you enable compression for a 100k token session").
- Compare with internal thread: slack/#long-context (search: "persistent-kv") — pull top action items.

References / seeds for reading list
- arXiv:2802.04567 — Temporal Retrieval for Dialog Memory
- NeurIPS 2027 short paper — Lossy Episodic Compression
- internal blog: Cost-aware Caching for LLM Serving (prod infra)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwoodinference/inference-runtime/pull/1234
- Confluence draft: CONF-9876 (context strategy brainstorm)

End — will iterate after the clarify-set is done and we have toy compressor results.

Benjamin
morning notes, 2028-04-03
